description: Dynamic Site Characterization of Soft Ground in Seattle: Workflow, Analysis and Results is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Joseph Wartman, University of Washington (washington.edu). Seattle is a city that underwent significant regrading as it expanded in the 1900s, resulting in fill materials with depths ranging from a few feet to over 200 feet. Many of the locations of fill material present the largest seismic hazards in the Seattle area; however, some areas are not well characterized. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-6xpj-6f76. Keywords: RAPID, HVSR, Site characterization, Seismic site response, Soil dynamics, Geotechnical engineering. Published 2022-09-06. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
